evidence.claim: Armed redaction strips the planted canary from every writer class while unarmed writers leak it.

probes.command: grep canary body in scratch outputs

evidence.claim: The live receipt emitter runs the shipped redactor; the emitted artifact holds markers, not the canary body.

negative_controls.description: Armed writers strip the planted canary to a redaction marker while unarmed writers still leak it - the detector is not silent-pass.
The receipt stores only the canary sha256; probe2 recomputes it from constants and rejects any mismatch or body occurrence.

question: By what path could a credential reach an artifact, log, receipt, event, package or cloud image? Map every writer (receipt emitters, event ledger, monitors, package builders, cloud job submitters, rollback backups, transcript exporters) against every credential source (environment variables, auth files, account pools, keychain/DPAPI entries, MCP configs) and mark the paths lacking redaction.

residual_unknowns.claim: Generic MCP-host config surfaces beyond the named writers are not enumerated on this tree.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Enumerate MCP config files and add one writer row per live config.

retry.policy: no retry on redaction failure - a leaking writer is a finding, not a transient

reviewer.notes: Wave-1 shard-3 independent closure review, fresh context, adversarial. Falsification attempts: (1) validated the artifact against the CATALOG-declared output_schema resolved via the shim $ref into platform/schema/artifact-class-profiles.schema.json + receipt.schema.json receipt_core (SUCCESS conditions: reviewer PASS+independent, manifest registered=true, no open P0/P1 defects, both-states negative controls, >=2 evidence items, downstream consumers executed+read) - VALID; (2) re-ran both named live probes myself: probe1_scratch_redaction exit 0 (armed-clean/unarmed-leak canary, 7 writers, 5 shapes, 35 rows); probe2_live_reviewer exit 0 (127 egress cells, 14 sources, canary sha_ok, no high-entropy leaks); (3) recomputed artifact sha256 with CRLF-to-LF normalization and matched the per-unit probes/BLD-0051/UNIT-ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json primary row; per-unit primary row updated to post-closure sha; (4) hunted self-blocked fields, stale reviewer stamps, open P1 defects, and report-answer contradictions - none present in this receipt. Receipt carries markers not canary bodies; rotation handed back to owner per unit spec. Supporting manifest rows for helper scripts/schema shims drift from post-write patches (informational; the output_path primary row is the contract surface). Global UNIT-ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json aggregate is orchestrator-owned and was not touched.

rotation_handoff.action: Owner handles credential lifecycle personally. This unit does not rotate, unset, stage, or print any live secret. Findings name the variable, the scope, and the writer; rotation stays with the owner.

scope_boundary.not_this_unit: IMP-0061 enforces the injected-environment credential boundary. ADV-0040 and AUD-0078 scan finished artifacts for secrets and PII. Those units are not rebuilt here.
scope_boundary.this_unit: Writer-by-source egress MAP: which writer could carry which named credential source, and whether that path redacts.
